newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures await U.S., German jobs data.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures await U.S., German jobs data.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were slightly firmer in early dealings on Friday, underpinned by leaks on Thursday that today's German jobless data would show ongoing high unemployment.
DTB September Bund futures were up three basis points at 100.53 points, while the 10-year benchmark Bund due July 2007 was at 101.27 percent for a yield of 5.82 percent.
"Friday should be called Employment Friday this week," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Futures & Options said in a commentary, noting the release at 0855 GMT of German data.
U.S. jobs data will follow at 1230 GMT.
The market on Thursday factored in the German data after official sources said the unadjusted jobless total fell 91,000 to 4.256 million, less than economists had been expecting.
"The market is spending much more of its time worrying about the U.S. data since the German data has already been in the market," said one trader.
On a technical basis, traders looked for September Bunds to find support at 100.44,. 100.18 before 100.00, while resistance was evident at 100.70 and 100.93.
